lines.text: Everything you've done so far happened in Tuner X, with no code at all. From here on you write it, and this page is the short list of Java you'll want first.
If Java is new to you, start with this free course. Four modules is plenty, and the third one is what the robot code leans on hardest.
Then stop. There's more Java after that, but nothing in this workshop uses it, and we'll fill in the rest as it comes up.
These six words show up in every lesson after this one. The course teaches five of them.
The constructor runs once, at the moment the arm is built. That makes it the place for anything that should only happen a single time, like setting up a motor.
The lambda is the odd one out. That little arrow turns the code after it into a parcel, written down and handed over instead of run.
You'll also call methods you can't find anywhere in your own file. One word on the class line is why, because the arm gets everything a mechanism can do without writing any of it.
Here's all of that in one real method from the arm. A name and a return type on top, then a lambda in the middle with dots chaining the calls around it.
This is the part people miss. Calling that method doesn't move the arm. You get a command back with the parcel inside, and it sits there until something else runs it.
Five questions tell you whether this stuck, so miss more than one and go back to the course. After that, you'll meet the thing that actually runs the command.
